LESSON: RUGBY

Grade: SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade 9
Subject: CREATIVE ARTS AND SPORTS
Strand: Creating and Performing
Topic 2.5: Rugby
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 10

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Rugby, part of Creating and Performing in SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade 9 CREATIVE ARTS AND SPORTS.

Key inquiry question: when demonstrating the skills. How is a ball advanced in a game of Rugby?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. Watch a live, or virtual Rugby game to identify passes (spin, pop and basic), and kicks (place and drop). Learners with postural defects or short stature could be appropriately positioned for comfort and clear view. Screen resolution and light intensity could be regulated for learners who are sensitive to light.

2. Demonstrate passing skills in Rugby. Safety precautions for all the learners should be observed with extra caution taken for learners with health conditions and those using mobility devices by ensuring that they move in safe environment

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. Watch a live, or virtual Rugby game to identify passes (spin, pop and basic), and kicks (place and drop). Learners with postural defects or short stature could be appropriately positioned for comfort and clear view. Screen resolution and light intensity could be regulated for learners who are sensitive to light.
2. Demonstrate passing skills in Rugby. Safety precautions for all the learners should be observed with extra caution taken for learners with health conditions and those using mobility devices by ensuring that they move in safe environment

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Rugby together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Communication and Collaboration: The learner communicates effectively by understanding and articulating the various

types of passes in Rugby.

• Digital Literacy: the learner interacts with digital devices to observe virtual performances in Rugby, to enhance digital

citizenship and appropriate use of technology.

• Creativity and Imagination: the learner devises creative ways of advancing the ball with passes to outsmart the opponents

during play and creatively model a dummy clay trophy.

Values:
• Integrity: The learner upholds a high standard of integrity by respecting the rules of the game and engaging in skill acquisition

with honesty and transparency.

• Unity: The learner actively collaborates with teammates, emphasising unity in executing passing drills to achieve collective

skill acquisition.

• Responsibility: as the learner adheres to safety guidelines and actively seeks opportunities to improve kicking skills.

27

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

• Health promotion issues- the learner enhances health and wellbeing while engaging in Rugby games to reduce the chances

of lifestyle diseases.

• Life skills - the learner develops the skill of coping with emotion when they play a modified Rugby game safely.

Link to other learning areas:

• Integrated Science: Exploring the science behind different kicking techniques incorporates principles of force, motion, and

anatomy.

• English: language skills are utilised when learners communicate and distinguish types of passes in Rugby, enhancing their

ability to express ideas clearly.
